thread:
incidents-bot: PAGING: potential third-party outage affecting Stripe webhook deliveries to our ingestion endpoints. Spike of 402/429 responses starting ~2026-03-15T09:06Z. Auto-created incident: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0315-stripe-ws
maya: oncall (maya) here — acknowledging, joining bridge now :phone: 09:09Z
sam: seeing failures in prod: webhook delivery success rate dropped from 99.8% -> 78% over last 20m. ~13.8k failed deliveries since 09:05Z. User-facing impact: new account creation flow stalls (webhook ack required) — ~1.1k signups errored in last 30m.
liam: I pulled raw responses — most are 429 rate_limit or 402 account_disabled with body:
```json
{"error":{"type":"account_disabled","message":"Account limited due to billing issue"}}
```
liam: Stripe status page shows no incident, but their response payload says account-limited. Could be account-level enforcement on our Stripe merchant account.
elaine: Finance note: we have a failed automatic payment on the primary Stripe account; collections team notified at 08:50Z, looks like Stripe flagged the account for quota enforcement. I'm pinging our Stripe AM and payments team now. cc @billing-bot
billing-bot: Finance ticket created: FIN-4521. Stripe AM contact queued — ETA response 20-40m.
kevin: mitigation ideas:
- short-term: queue inbound webhooks into internal durable queue (kafka/topic: stripe-delivery-retry) and return 202 -> reduce client retries
- enable offline-processing mode for signup flow (allow account creation with pending payment) via feature flag: ff.allow_signup_pending_payment = true
- adjust retry/backoff on webhook workers to exponential backoff up to 24h
maya: agree with Kevin. Can we flip the ff and queue quickly? How risky to return 202 to Stripe (we may need to ack to stop retries)?
sam: returning 202 harmless — Stripe will consider the webhook delivered. But we must persist raw payloads to retry later. Current pipeline drops failed attempts; need fast patch to store to s3/kafka.
kevin: I can push a small patch to the delivery lambda to persist to s3 then return 202. Will deploy behind canary to one region first. Patch outline:
```bash
# pseudocode
POST /webhook -> persist raw to s3://redwood-incoming/stripe/<ts>.json then return 202
```
kevin: starting PR and small canary deploy. ETA 12m.
maya: assigning ops tasks:
- @kevin: implement persist+202 canary (in progress)
- @sam: monitor queue + metrics (failure rate, retry queue depth)
- @eli(elaine): escalate finance ticket to get Stripe account re-enabled
- @liam: check for any other API keys/accounts affected
opsbridge-bot: Bridge created: https://zoom/ops-1879876543 (pw in DM). Oncall handoff channel created.
sam: adding temporary dashboard: webhook_fail_rate, failed_webhooks_count, signup_error_count, queue_depth (new). Posting link when ready.
liam: quick check — no other vendors showing similar failures (observability vendor, auth provider OK). This looks contained to our Stripe merchant account.
elaine: Stripe AM replied: they're reviewing account status, flagged for overdue invoices. They've escalated to internal collections. Stripe estimates 30-90m for resolution depending on payment confirmation.
maya: impact assessment: degraded — signups fallback unavailable until webhooks processed. Existing customers unaffected for most payment flows except some billing webhooks. Severity: P2 (customer-visible but not full outage). Notify CS: possible delayed access for new signups.
sam: numbers update 09:30Z: failed deliveries 17.2k, signup failures 1.9k. Queue depth (after kevin's canary) ~400 per minute incoming; persistence working on canary region.
kevin: canary deployed to us-east-1. Persist to s3+kafka enabled. Rolling to us-west next if metrics look stable. Returning 202 now for canary traffic.
maya: good. Flip ff.allow_signup_pending_payment = true in canary, then global if no regressions.
kevin: rolled ff in canary, seeing 0 signup errors in canary traffic; global rollout start in 6m.
sam: monitoring: overall failed deliveries still high (Stripe still returning 402/429) but our ingestion now accepting and persisting payloads. Queue backlog ~9k items accumulating.
elaine: finance: payment attempt in progress. I'll update FIN-4521 when confirmed.
billing-bot: Stripe payment confirmed at 10:03Z according to Stripe AM (message: "payment applied; account re-enabled"). Recommend waiting 5-10m for webhook backfill attempts to succeed.
liam: after Stripe confirmed, we're starting to see fewer 402 bodies; 429s still sporadic while they catch up. Retrying persisted payloads now using controlled backoff.
sam: replay job started at 10:08Z with concurrency 20, target 500/min to avoid re-triggering rate limits. Observed successful replays: 2.2k in first 10m.
maya: customer comms draft: "We're seeing delayed account activations due to third-party payment provider enforcement. We've implemented a temporary mode to allow account creation and are replaying queued webhooks. Most affected customers will gain access within a few minutes to a couple hours. Our teams are monitoring." Anybody object? quick ack :thumbsup:
kevin: :thumbsup:
liam: :thumbsup:
elaine: :thumbsup:
maya: timeline/status update for incident page: started 09:06Z, mitigation (persist+202 + pending-payment mode) deployed 09:22Z canary, 09:40Z global. Stripe confirmed payment 10:03Z. Replay underway. Estimated full catch-up 11:30Z. Severity P2 -> monitoring. Will keep bridge open until backlog drained. handing off to night oncall (liam) at 11:00Z.
liam: taking handoff at 11:00Z. Will monitor replay progress and queue drain. If Stripe returns renewed rate limits, escalate to AM for throttling window.
maya: thanks everyone. Postmortem owners: sam (technical mitigation), elaine + finance (billing/process), kevin (ingestion fix), liam (oncall follow-up). Please add action items to INC-2026-0315 and assign owners. Closing bridge when backlog <100 and customer-impacted signups count <10 over 30m.
opsbridge-bot: Bridge closed at 12:05Z by liam. Final note: backlog fully processed at 12:02Z, total persisted items: 28,742, replays succeeded: 28,720, failed replays: 22 (requeued for manual review). Incident moved to postmortem queue.
maya: adding follow-up: review billing automation to avoid auto-limiting (finance automation), add health-check on merchant billing status to surface earlier, and add automated safe-ack path (persist+202) as a default for webhook pipeline.
